questions.q: ___ tired, she went to bed early.
questions.explanation: A present participle clause shows the reason: 'because she felt tired'.

questions.q: The man ___ by the door is my uncle.
questions.explanation: A reduced relative clause uses the present participle for an active meaning.

questions.q: ___ in 1900, the bridge is still in use.
questions.explanation: A past participle clause gives a passive meaning.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Not know what to do, I called my mother.
Not knowing what to do, I called my mother.
Not known what to do, I called my mother.
Not to know what to do, I called my mother.
questions.explanation: A negative participle clause starts with 'not + -ing'.

questions.q: The girl ___ next to me is my cousin.
questions.explanation: Use the present participle to reduce 'who is sitting'.

questions.q: ___ the instructions, he assembled the furniture.
questions.explanation: 'Having + past participle' shows one action finished before another.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Exhausted by the journey, they fell asleep immediately.
Exhausting by the journey, they fell asleep immediately.
Exhaust by the journey, they fell asleep immediately.
Being exhausted by the journey, they fell asleep immediately.
questions.explanation: A past participle clause describes a passive state.

questions.q: The book ___ on the table is mine.
questions.explanation: Use the present participle of 'lie' (rest), not 'lay'.

questions.q: ___ all the evidence, the jury reached a verdict.
questions.explanation: 'Having considered' shows the considering came first.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Shocking by the news, she couldn't speak.
Shocked by the news, she couldn't speak.
Shock by the news, she couldn't speak.
Being shocking by the news, she couldn't speak.
questions.explanation: A past participle clause expresses a passive reaction.

questions.q: People ___ in this area often complain about noise.
questions.explanation: Reduce 'who live' to the present participle 'living'.

questions.q: ___ late, he missed the beginning.
questions.explanation: A present participle clause means 'because he arrived late'.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Known for his honesty, he was trusted by everyone.
Knowing for his honesty, he was trusted by everyone.
Know for his honesty, he was trusted by everyone.
Being known for his honesty, he was trusted by everyone.
questions.explanation: A past participle clause gives the passive reason 'because he was known'.

questions.q: The documents ___ yesterday have arrived.
questions.explanation: Reduce 'which were signed' to the past participle.

questions.q: ___ his keys, he couldn't get in.
questions.explanation: 'Having lost' shows the losing happened before he arrived.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Walk home, I met an old friend.
Walked home, I met an old friend.
To walk home, I met an old friend.
Walking home, I met an old friend.
questions.explanation: A present participle clause means 'while I was walking home'.

questions.q: Anyone ___ in the course should register now.
questions.explanation: Use the past participle 'interested' for the passive feeling.

questions.q: ___ by her parents, she felt more confident.
questions.explanation: A past participle clause gives the passive cause.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Have finished his work, he went for a walk.
Finished his work, he went for a walk.
Having finish his work, he went for a walk.
Having finished his work, he went for a walk.
questions.explanation: 'Having finished' shows the work came before the walk.

questions.q: The train ___ at platform 2 is delayed.
questions.explanation: Reduce 'which is waiting' to the present participle.
